content.title: UFL Moves Away From Memphis, Michigan, San Antonio Markets
content.text: As expected, the UFL has finally announced their plans to move away from a few of their markets for 2026. Memphis, Michigan, and San Antonio will be relocated to new cities next season. The Official Press Release reads as follows: The United Football League is committed to delivering the most accessible and innovative football experience every spring. This offseason, in partnership with our new ownership group, we’ve refreshed our vision for the league with a focus on playing in more intimate venues that elevate the fan experience and bring unmatched energy to game day. As part of this process, we conducted a thorough review of all markets and venues. After careful consideration, we’ve made the difficult decision to depart from the Memphis, Michigan, and San Antonio markets. Unfortunately, the stadium options currently available in these areas do not align with our new vision. As we look ahead to potential expansion in 2028, we remain hopeful that the right venues will become available in these markets so we can return and once again bring UFL football to these communities. Further details about the league’s new markets and venues will be shared in an announcement next week.See also Thank you for being a fan and joining us on this journey. We can’t wait to kick off an incredible 2026 season with you in March! Quick Thoughts These moves aren’t too surprising for the most part. We reported back in July that the UFL was planning to relocate four teams. Things changed with Mike Repole at the helm, though, as Birmingham stayed put – and now Houston gets to maintain a place in the league over San Antonio. The early word for the three new markets: Columbus, Louisville, and Orlando. We will keep the public informed as we hear more. What are your thoughts on Memphis, Michigan, and San Antonio losing their UFL teams? Let us know down in the comments below, or join the conversation on Discord!
